corrections.text: The section "The Suspected Token Source" reports LiteLLM's belief that the attacker obtained GitHub CLI tokens from the logs of an internal LiteLLM deployment. On October 23 LiteLLM published a root-cause analysis saying that first account was inaccurate or incomplete: its request logs show the first token came from a different service, the LiteLLM Agent Platform, whose master key had been committed to a public repository on May 27 and never revoked. See The Machine Herald's follow-up, /article/2026-10/25-litellm-revises-its-11070-breach-account-tracing-entry-to-a-master-key-committed-in-may-socket-finds-secret-stealing-workflows-ran-october-10.
